SMTO-EXE-0118 — SMTO can't use that part of the page right now

GUID: 4666aa3e-aeee-5070-948e-d7beb228ded5
Slug: browser-element-not-interactable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO found the item but couldn't use it the way it was asked, for example the button is greyed out, hidden, or isn't a box you can type in. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to look at the page and tell you why the item might be unavailable, such as a greyed-out button or a pop-up covering it. SMTO only acts on items that are visible and switched on.
  2. If the page needs something first, such as ticking a box, filling a required field or closing a pop-up, ask SMTO to do that first. Many sites keep a button disabled until the form is complete.
  3. When SMTO should type, tell it the text box to use, not the label or button next to it. Typing only works in a box that accepts text.
  4. When uploading, tell SMTO to use the site's file chooser or Upload field itself. A file can only be added through the page's file chooser, not a nearby button or link.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the click, typing or upload, and the page shows the result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with a description of the page, to the person who manages SMTO. Some sites block automated use of certain controls.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The target browser element is not visible or not enabled, is not editable for fill/type_text, or is not a file input for upload_file.

What this means

  • The exact target was not visible/enabled, was not editable for text entry, or was not a file input for upload. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • The exact target was not visible/enabled, was not editable for text entry, or was not a file input for upload.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect visibility, enabled state and semantic control type without forcing an interaction through the guard.

How to fix it

  • PlaywrightBackend._target raises element_not_interactable when the handle fails is_visible() or is_enabled(); execute raises it when fill/type_text targets a non-editable element or upload_file targets anything other than an input element of type file. Inspect the page with browser.snapshot, satisfy whatever enables the control, and target an element of the correct type.
  • Inspect the page and select a visible enabled element of the correct control type.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the page and select a visible enabled element of the correct control type.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended control becomes available and supports the exact requested action.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
